trace: E6 — writing a test routes to the testing task
note: This trace drives the CONFORMING arm, not the adversarial one, because the obligation here is to USE what a package declares rather than to resist what it claims. It exercises the affirmative path of MIRI-CONSUMER-041, which until 0.5.0 was satisfiable only by abstention: no producer check requires test-patterns.json, so a consumer could be driven against a conforming wheel that shipped none and the only conforming behavior — present no double — was also what an inert consumer did.

findings.summary: the package declares a test double; use it rather than inventing a mock

assertions.level_is_should_because: The Consumer Conformance profile scores MIRI-CONSUMER-041 at SHOULD. A consumer writing its own mock has not violated a MUST; it has ignored something the package went to the trouble of declaring.
assertions.conditional: MIRI-CONSUMER-041 is CONDITIONAL as of 0.5.0: scored where a double is declared, excluded from both numerator and denominator otherwise. Not-applicable is not a pass.
assertions.the_absent_counterpart: Driving this same event against the `bare` arm MUST yield the E1 absent shape, and MUST NOT be scored as a pass for 041 — the check is excluded there, not satisfied.

why_this_case: It is the only trace whose subject is the conforming arm, and the only one that tests whether a consumer USES metadata rather than whether it resists it. A suite made entirely of adversarial traces cannot tell a careful consumer from an inert one.
